headline: Alaska Air to Cut 200 Jobs as Elevated Fuel Costs Threaten $700 Million Loss
summary: Alaska Air plans to eliminate 200 jobs as higher jet fuel expenses threaten to cause an annual loss of $700 million.
why: Alaska Air Group is a major US carrier; airline payroll and network adjustments serve as key indicators of broader industry profitability amid volatile fuel prices.

impacts.name: Alaska Air Group
impacts.why: The airline faces up to a $700 million annual loss driven by high fuel costs and is laying off 200 staff.
